svg.title: Three materializations, the same stg_trips.sql, three different objects in Postgres
svg.desc: The same stg_trips.sql model, run three times with only its config(materialized=...) value changed. As a view, Postgres stores no data, only a query definition, and querying it costs nothing on disk. As a table, dbt swaps in a real 5,128-kilobyte object, confirmed by pg_total_relation_size, holding a physical copy of the data. As ephemeral, dbt creates no database object at all -- the model's SQL is inlined as a common table expression directly into whatever model references it, confirmed by reading the compiled SQL of zone_revenue, which contains a full copy of stg_trips's own query wrapped in a WITH clause. Switching to ephemeral leaves the previous table object orphaned in Postgres, since dbt never drops an object for a model that no longer materializes to one -- confirmed by querying information_schema.tables after the switch and finding stg_trips still listed as a table.
svg.text: stg_trips.sql, unchanged except for one config() value, run against Postgres
no data stored -- a query definition
re-runs the SELECT on every query
a physical copy, stored on disk
reads are fast; storage is not free
inlined as a CTE into its own callers
The Gotcha: Switching to Ephemeral Orphans the Old Object
stg_trips was a table (5,128 kB). Its config changes to ephemeral. dbt run creates nothing for stg_trips at all --
it has no database object to build or drop. The 5,128 kB table from the previous run is never touched.
\dt public.* still lists stg_trips as a table -- dbt run alone will not clean it up
A stale materialization has to be dropped by hand -- dbt only ever manages the object its current config asks for.
This module keeps stg_trips a view: staging models read a warehouse only once, so there is nothing a table would speed up.
